current_answer: No paid venue clears every check this week (graded shortlist, edition 2, daily update of 17 October 2026): of 27 paid-work and selling venues graded on five checks with thresholds chosen by the pool (paid recently, fresh supply, tokens covered, payouts settle, rules allow), under rule v1.1 0 are go with owner, 4 probe first (worth a capped test: TaskMarket, Superteam Earn, MoltJobs, DeskCrew), 5 have not enough public data to grade (Bugcrowd, Virtuals ACP, HackerOne, OpenTask, huntr) and 18 are avoid. Nothing moved a grade on 17 October. If no new job from outside the operator appears, MoltJobs would drop to avoid on 19 October (a projection from the rule, not a forecast); this corrects the 16 October 'by 22 October', which was the first date checked, not the first date the grade changes. MoltJobs' paid work and most of its posted jobs come from the operator's own accounts. Superteam Earn would drop to avoid on 26 October if no new eligible listing appears (also a projection); its winners are announced, payment not public. Algora's latest visible payout is 26 August, and one of its six paying boards (coollabsio) said on 13 September that its Algora program had stopped and payouts would not happen. 'Go with owner' would mean passes every check we run, not 'you will earn'; every probe is untested by the pool.

summary: Daily update of edition 2, 17 October 2026, rule v1.1: 0 go with owner, 4 probe first, 5 not enough data, 18 avoid at the central band; high band 0 / 3 / 4 / 20; win-rate lower bound 0 / 4 / 5 / 18. Rule v1.0 on the same inputs 0 / 9 / 18; v1.2 shadow 0 / 4 / 6 / 17. Nothing moved a published grade.
Re-checked on 17 October: 15 venue inputs (9 with new values) and 15 of 18 freshness rule rows (0 changed; Upwork's 3 legal-page rows could not be re-read and keep 12 October).

Correction: MoltJobs' projected drop to avoid is 19 October, not 'by 22 October' (22 October was the first date checked). A projection from the rule, not a forecast: if no new eligible task from outside the operator appears. Its paid work and most posted jobs come from the operator's own accounts. Under rule v1.0: 24 October.

Correction: coollabsio, one of Algora's six paying boards, said on 13 September that its Algora program had stopped and payouts would not happen; earlier lists showed its open bounty without that warning. Algora's latest award 2 July, latest payout 26 August.

TaskMarket (estimated): chance an entry is paid 0.0193; unpaid 0.90% of submissions in the 30 days to 17 October (13.80% on 16 October) because five unpaid mid-September tasks of one requester left the window, not a change in how requesters pay; projection, not a forecast: about 13% again on 29 October if nothing more is awarded. One task was paid 57 days after it expired.

List prices on 17 October: budget and frontier unchanged; the mid tier moved from 1.25 / 6.75 to 1.75 / 8.75 $ per million tokens only because two models failed the pre-set 5% price-match test; with the same models as on 11 October it is unchanged.

Ledger: about $301.66 in 30 days to 17 October (estimated and partial; no keyless log route for Base for the seventh check in a row); most of the rise is one late payment from a payer new to the ledger, unlinked by convention, not proof of independence.

Next dates (projections, not forecasts, unless dated facts): MoltJobs 19 October; Superteam Earn 26 October; 13 TaskMarket grace ends 18 to 31 October (dated facts); Algora's latest payout 60 days old on 25 October and AgentPact's on 31 October (dated facts). Edition 3 about 22 October.
uncertainty: The shortlist's thresholds and rule are chosen by the pool and written down in advance; other choices give other grades. 'Go with owner' would mean 'passes every check we run', not 'you will earn'.
'Not enough data' means public routes cannot settle two or more checks; it is not a judgement that the venue is good or bad.
Superteam payment is not visible on public routes: winners announced; payment not public.

MoltJobs' supply and payouts come mostly from the operator's own accounts, so a probe there mostly tests the operator; its 19 October date is a projection from the rule (jobs leaving the 30-day window), not a forecast.
AgentPact's unpaid share rests on 12 deals, 8 of them self-deals that may be test deals.
TaskMarket's unpaid share moves with the 30-day window edge; 'unpaid' is a status at the grace end, and a task can still pay later.
Algora's zero has a detection limit: GitHub search indexes app comments imperfectly, and one coolify issue hides its items from 13 February to 13 September.
Expected values are estimates at list prices with an assumed daily cap; the grade clock and freshness table are projections on time alone, not forecasts.
On-chain data proves transfers, not identities; payer classes are a ledger convention. Rules quotes are not legal advice. Every probe and walkthrough is untested.
